wa_austrian_slab.blurb: Austrian Slab is a slab-style crag inside Peshastin Pinnacles State Park, near Leavenworth and Wenatchee. It holds about a dozen routes, roughly two thirds trad and the rest sport, running from easy 5.7 up to a lone 5.11, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10. The sandstone here is soft in places, and many of the bolted lines are bold with long gaps between protection, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on slabs and a little run-out. Several routes are rated well, but the rock on some upper pitches is poor and parties often finish after the first pitch. The base is easy to find, and you can come down by rappel or scrambling off to the left.

wa_e_the_velvet.blurb: The Velvet is a crack-focused wall on the upper west side of Lookout Point at Index, in the Skykomish Valley of the west Cascades. Nearly all of its routes are trad, with a single sport line, and they range from 5.9 into the 5.12 range, most of them 5.9 and 5.10. Several are multi-pitch, and the longest takes five pitches. The granodiorite faces are open to the sun, so hot midday hours are best avoided, while the top of the wall is shady and has a pleasant view. The wall is reached by climbing the first pitch of one of the neighbouring multi-pitch routes. It suits climbers comfortable with crack protection.

wa_five_fun_wall.blurb: Five Fun Wall is a small bolted sport crag in the Tum Tum climbing area, about an hour west of Spokane. All thirteen routes are sport climbs, short and well protected, and most sit between 5.7 and 5.8, with a handful at 5.9 and 5.10 and two 5.11 routes for those wanting a harder test. That spread makes it a friendly place for newer leaders and for a relaxed warm-up before heading to the harder crags nearby. The wall is a short stroll from the parking area, reached by following the trail north. Watch for poison ivy and rattlesnakes in warm months.

wi_4_flatiron.blurb: The Flatiron is a bouldering area high on the East Bluff at Devil's Lake, in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range. It sits along the trail up from the CCC area, on the cliff band just below the top of the bluff. Thirteen problems are spread across a wide range, from easy V1 and V2 lines through a middle group around V4, up to hard V7 to V9 problems, with one standout far beyond the rest. A few of them are classics, and some are tall, so pads and spotters matter. The boulders are quick to reach on foot from the trail, which makes the spot popular for a short session.

wi_1_misery_rocks.blurb: Misery Rocks is a formation at the south end of Devil's Lake's West Bluff, reached on foot up the West Bluff Trail. It is one of the most beginner-friendly places at the lake: most of its thirteen climbs are easy to moderate trad or top-rope lines, from about 5.2 up to a few 5.9 and 5.10 routes. The base has a flat area to gather, and the woods around the rock give plenty of shade in summer. Weekends can be busy, particularly with guided groups, so try the neighbouring formations when it is crowded. Most routes need gear placements or a top-rope anchor, since the lake has no bolted lines.

wi_01_prospect_point_pinnacle.blurb: Prospect Point Pinnacle is a small freestanding cliff at the southern end of the Prospect Point Rampart on Devil's Lake's West Bluff, in the Baraboo Range. It is a short walk along the West Bluff Trail from the junction with the service road. The thirteen routes are mostly trad with a few top-rope lines, running from easy 5.2 climbs to a couple of 5.9 and 5.10 routes, with a good number of moderate faces and corners in between. The base can be reached by a climbers' path just south of the pinnacle, or by rappel. It is a quieter, smaller option than the long cliffs further north on the rampart.

wi_3_the_frigate.blurb: The Frigate is a ship-shaped formation on the West Bluff at Devil's Lake, just above Porkchop Buttress and Dungeon Wall. All thirteen routes are trad. They start at an easy 5.3 and run up through a cluster of 5.8 to 5.10 lines to one 5.12 test piece, with the 5.5 on the formation a popular pick. The overhanging west wall gives the steepest climbing, and another overhanging face lies to the southeast. The walk to the top is by trail through the woods from the West Bluff Trail, and there is a scramble route up the back that works for setting or retrieving top-rope anchors.
